public_rationale: The research supports concern about unreliable causal answers in language models. It also documents successful specialist causal methods. These findings do not settle whether existing approaches collectively were inadequate in December 2022. Calling the claim supported would require generalizing from limited evaluations; calling it contradicted would require treating specialist success as sufficient for an unstated standard of adequacy.
limitations: The cited experiments and theoretical results are historical context, not comprehensive measurements within the target month.
A narrower claim about language-model reliability would be easier to assess than this claim about current approaches generally.

evidence.explanation: The study reports unstable causal-graph answers, but also GPT-3 successes on 11 of 15 abstract questions and 21 of 36 intuitive-physics questions. Its limited model coverage and unspecified experiment dates prevent treating it as a comprehensive December 2022 outcome test.

The paper develops an algorithm for determining whether causal effects are identifiable and estimating them when they are, given structural constraints. This challenges a reading that existing approaches were uniformly ineffective, but does not demonstrate broad autonomous causal reasoning in December 2022.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative historical evaluation of December 2022 approaches across causal relationships, interventions, and counterfactuals, with an adequacy standard justified independently of the results.
